'''MedCalc''' is a statistical software package designed for the biomedical sciences.<ref>{{cite book |first1=Jin-Ho |last1=Chun |year=2014 |title=DR Chun's 'Edge' Health·Medical Statistics, 2 LEAD or 2 be leaded? |publisher=Panmun Education |location=Seoul | isbn=979-11-85305-57-8 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first1=Li |last1=Zhihui |first2=Du |last2=Zhicheng |year=2018 |title=MedCalc Statistical Analysis Methodology and Application/Statistical Analysis Series Paperback |publisher=Publishing House of Electronics Industry |location=Beijing | isbn=978-7121338694 |edition=Chinese }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author=Eunsil Choi, Jiyoung Lyu, Jinyoung Park, Hae-Young Kim |title=Statistical methods used in articles published by the Journal of Periodontal and Implant Science |journal=Journal of Periodontal & Implant Science |volume=44 |year=2014 |pages=288–292 |pmid=25568809 | pmc=4284377 |doi=10.5051/jpis.2014.44.6.288 |issue=6}}</ref> The first version of MedCalc, for [[MS-DOS]], was released in April 1993, then a [[Windows]] version in November 1996.

It has an integrated spreadsheet for data input and can import files in several formats ([[Microsoft Excel|Excel]], [[SPSS]], [[Comma-separated values|CSV]]).

MedCalc includes basic parametric and [[non-parametric]] statistical procedures and graphs such as [[descriptive statistics]], [[ANOVA]], [[Mann–Whitney U test|Mann–Whitney test]], [[Wilcoxon signed-rank test|Wilcoxon test]], [[chi-squared distribution|χ<sup>2</sup> test]], [[correlation]], [[linear regression|linear]] as well as [[Nonlinear regression|non-linear regression]], [[logistic regression]], and multivariate statistics.<ref>{{cite book |first1=K.V.S. |last1=Sarma |first2=Rudravaram |last2=Vishnu Vardhan |year=2018 |title=Multivariate Statistics Made Simple: A Practical Approach |publisher=Chapman & Hall/CRC |location=Boca Raton, FL | isbn=978-0-4298-7787-2 }}</ref>

Survival analysis includes Cox regression ([[Proportional hazards model]]) and [[Kaplan–Meier estimator|Kaplan–Meier]] survival analysis.

Procedures for method evaluation and method comparison include [[ROC curve]] analysis,<ref>{{cite book |first1=Wojtek J. |last1=Krzanowski |first2=David J. |last2=Hand |year=2009 |title=ROC Curves for Continuous Data |publisher=Chapman & Hall/CRC |location=Boca Raton, FL | isbn=978-1-4398-0021-8 }}</ref> [[Bland–Altman plot]],<ref>{{cite journal |author=Hanneman SK |title=Design, analysis, and interpretation of method-comparison studies |journal=AACN Advanced Critical Care |volume=19 |year=2008 |pages=223–234 |pmid=18560291 |doi=10.1097/01.AACN.0000318125.41512.a3 |issue=2 |pmc=2944826}}</ref> as well as [[Deming regression|Deming]] and [[Passing–Bablok regression]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Lidija Bilić-Zulle |title=Comparison of methods: Passing and Bablok regression |journal= Biochemia Medica|volume=21 |year=2011 |pages=49–52 |doi=10.11613/BM.2011.010 |issue=1|pmid=22141206 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

The software also includes reference interval estimation,<ref>{{cite journal |author=Bosa Mirjanic-Azaric, Sanja Avram, Tanja Stojakovic-Jelisavac, Darja Stojanovic, Mira Petkovic, Natasa Bogavac-Stanojevic, Svetlana Ignjatovic, and Marina Stojanov |title=Direct Estimation of Reference Intervals for Thyroid Parameters in the Republic of Srpska |journal=Journal of Medical Biochemistry |volume=36 |year=2017 |pages=137–144 |doi=10.1515/jomb-2017-0008 |issue=2 | pmid=28680357 | pmc=5471646}}</ref>  [[meta-analysis]] and sample size calculations.

Version 15.2 introduced a user-interface in English, Chinese (simplified and traditional), French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese (Brazilian), Russian and Spanish.
